title: How Plants Grow
passages: A seed may look small and still, but inside it waits a tiny plant with its own supply of stored food. When the soil turns damp and warm, the seed soaks up water and swells until its tough outer coat splits open. This waking up is called GERMINATION. First a root pushes downward, anchoring the young plant and drinking from the soil. Then a pale shoot bends upward, searching for light. Until it reaches the surface, the seedling lives entirely on the food packed inside the seed, much like a traveler living on what was carried from home.

Once its first leaves open, the plant begins making its own food. Leaves are green because of CHLOROPHYLL, a substance that catches sunlight. Using that energy, the plant combines water pulled up from its roots with carbon dioxide, a gas it takes in through tiny openings called STOMATA. This process, PHOTOSYNTHESIS, produces sugar for growth and releases oxygen into the air we breathe. People around the world have found clever ways to help plants get what they need, from terraced hillsides that hold rainwater to rooftop gardens reaching toward the sun.
